bibliographic-data.invention-title: CLOSED-LOOP THERMODYNAMIC CAVITATION AND NANOSECOND PULSED PLASMA REACTOR SYSTEM AND MULTI-DOMAIN APPLICATIONS THEREOF

description.p: This international PCT application claims priority to U.S. Patent Applications CPC-PAT-2026-001 through CPC-PAT-2026-013-CIP, encompassing 77 claims and 26 figures across 24 sheets.

The Cool Power Core (CPC) reactor (100) bridges low-grade waste, metabolic, geothermal, planetary, or directed-energy thermal enthalpy against ambient or cryogenic cold sinks via a 90°C fluid reservoir (102), a CVD-graphene vortex cavitation chamber (104), a 33.6 kV ZVS nanosecond pulsed plasma zone (106), and a phase-change condenser (108) exporting +286.0 to +368.5 We continuous power and 12.96 L/day pure condensate per core.

Further embodiments disclosed across FIGS. 1–26 include isotopic radiolytic cogeneration (400), wearable metabolic exoskeletons (500), tri-necked continuum robotic mounts (800), peer-to-peer 48 VDC / 90°C swarm couplers (1000), handheld planetary plasma lances (1200), abyssal hydrothermal torches and zero-recoil asteroid rock-splitters (1400, 1500), atmospheric terraforming spires and sub-glacial cryo-volcanic rovers (1600, 1700), evacuated terrestrial and subsea maglev conduits (1800, 1900), floating zero-brine ocean hubs and orbital artificial-gravity colonies (2000, 2100), radiation-shielded linear ridge-and-valley subterranean megastructures (2200), kinetic/DEW-harvesting viscoelastic-TPV power armor (2400), and quad-mode atmospheric-condensing rifles with under-barrel magnetic-mirror plasma bayonets and Bitter-coil heat recuperation (2500, 2600).

claim.claim-text: 1. Closed-loop thermodynamic cavitation and nanosecond pulsed plasma reactor (100) comprising a 90°C fluid reservoir (102), a CVD-graphene vortex cavitation chamber (104), a 33.6 kV zero-voltage-switching nanosecond plasma discharge zone (106), and a phase-change condenser (108) exporting net electrical power and distilled condensate.

2. The reactor (100) of claim 1, wherein the CVD-graphene vortex cavitation chamber (104) operates at a hydrodynamic cavitation number between 0.08 and 0.14 to generate sonoluminescent radical micro-bubbles.

3. The reactor (100) of claim 1, wherein the 33.6 kV nanosecond pulsed plasma exciter (106) delivers sub-15 ns rise-time pulses at 10–50 kHz to dissociate water and organic contaminants without bulk thermal runaway.
4. The reactor (100) of claim 1, further comprising a Sm2Co17 Halbach magnetic flux concentrator (110) surrounding the plasma discharge zone (106) to stabilize electron cyclotron resonance.
5. The reactor (100) of claim 1, wherein the phase-change condenser (108) couples across a thermoelectric and micro-Rankine recuperator (112) to export +286.0 to +368.5 We continuous per core.
6. The reactor (100) of claim 1, further comprising a catalytic ozone/NOx tail-gas scrubber (114) and a mineral ash trap (116) achieving 6-Log (99.9999%) PFAS and pathogen mineralization.

7. A method of simultaneous power cogeneration and zero-liquid-discharge water purification comprising preheating feedstock to 90°C (102), inducing hydrodynamic cavitation (104), applying 33.6 kV nanosecond plasma pulses (106), and condensing purified distillate (108).
8. The method of claim 7, wherein industrial waste enthalpy of 382.93 Wth per core offsets external heating energy to achieve a thermodynamic enthalpy recovery ratio above 88%.
9. The method of claim 7, further comprising separating electrolytic H2 and USP-grade O2 (118) from the plasma-cavitation vapor stream.

10. A modular zero-septic residential utility appliance (200) incorporating one or more reactors (100) of claim 1 to convert household greywater and blackwater into potable distillate and grid-interactive microgrid electricity.
11. The appliance (200) of claim 10, further comprising a 50-micron rotary solids cyclone (202) and an ASSE 1013 double-air-gap sanitary isolation manifold (204).
12. The appliance (200) of claim 10, recovering at least 98.5% of influent residential wastewater as <1 ppm TDS potable water while supplying 55°C domestic hot water (206).
13. The appliance (200) of claim 10, housed within a NEMA 4X outdoor enclosure (208) operating below 36 dBA with automated mineral cartridge replacement.

14. A radiation-hardened cogeneration reactor (400) integrating 4H-SiC and CVD-diamond alpha/beta/gamma-voltaic liners (402) within the cavitation-plasma core (100) to harvest ionizing radiation alongside waste thermal enthalpy.
15. The reactor (400) of claim 14, utilizing radiolytic radical generation to reduce nanosecond plasma electrical excitation draw below 15.5 W per core.
16. The reactor (400) of claim 14, further comprising a Pd-23%Ag permeation membrane (404) for continuous tritium and deuterium fuel-cycle recovery.

17. A wearable powered exoskeleton life-support system (500) comprising a dorsal micro-reactor (502) bridging 37°C human metabolic heat against ambient cold sinks to supply joint actuator power, O2, and recycled hydration.
18. The exoskeleton (500) of claim 17, incorporating closed-loop urinary and perspiration plasma distillation (504) for >480 hours of sealed EVA endurance.
19. The exoskeleton (500) of claim 17, wherein regenerative joint braking enthalpy is routed directly into the 90°C thermal reservoir (506).
20. A method of sustaining a sealed planetary EVA suit using metabolic enthalpy (37°C) and nanosecond plasma radiolysis to regenerate breathable oxygen and potable water.
21. The method of claim 20, maintaining cabin/suit relative humidity at 48% ± 3% and CO2 below 450 ppm.
22. An autonomous biomimetic robotic platform (800) powered by an internal micro-reactor (802) harvesting actuator QDD waste heat to generate continuous electricity, distilled water, and oxygen.

23. The platform (800) of claim 22, configured as a heavy quadruped mount (804) featuring three telescoping omni-flexible continuum manipulator necks (806) terminating in convertible sensor-hand effectors (808).
24. The platform (804) of claim 23, further comprising deployable ballistic shield wings (810) and an 8-DOF prehensile utility tail (812).
25. A closed-loop robotic thermal-to-electric drivetrain converting stator copper and core losses directly into 90°C cavitation-plasma fluid enthalpy.
26. The drivetrain of claim 25, utilizing a 48 VDC graphene-CNT supercapacitor buffer (814) for multi-kilowatt peak locomotion bursts.
27. A peer-to-peer robotic and modular utility docking interface (1000) providing simultaneous 48 VDC bidirectional power transfer and 90°C closed-loop fluid thermal sharing.
28. The interface (1000) of claim 27, employing self-sealing dry-break Ti-6Al-4V fluid couplings (1002) and magnetic alignment latches (1004).
29. The interface (1000) of claim 27, enabling autonomous swarm load-balancing across heterogeneous residential, mobile, and stationary cores.
30. A method of forming an ad-hoc microgrid and district thermal bus by autonomously docking multiple Cool Power Core units via dual-bus couplers (1000).
31. The method of claim 30, executing automated impedance matching and enthalpy priority routing within 50 milliseconds of mechanical latch engagement.

32. A handheld planetary plasma lance (1200) powered by a closed-loop cavitation-plasma core (1202) rejecting heat through external cryo-fins (1204) to sustain a magnetically confined plasma blade (1206).
33. The plasma lance (1200) of claim 32, wherein a 0.42 T Sm2Co17 Halbach array (1208) and a +0.23 T Bitter electromagnet coil (1210) generate a 0.65 T throat and 0.67 T distal magnetic mirror pinch.
34. The plasma lance (1200) of claim 32, further comprising a coaxial vapor aspiration shroud (1212) recovering >98% of ionized working fluid back into the 90°C reservoir.
35. The plasma lance (1200) of claim 32, regenerating +142.0 We continuous power against a -60°C Martian ambient sink to recharge an internal 140 Wh graphene-CNT supercapacitor (1214).
36. The plasma lance (1200) of claim 32, incorporating a capacitive EVA-glove deadman sensor (1216) triggering GaN solid-state magnetic quench in <1.2 milliseconds.
37. The plasma lance (1200) of claim 32, operable across permafrost boring, Ti-6Al-4V welding, and emergency airlock breach modes from a 180 mL water/ice cartridge (1218).

38. An abyssal hydrothermal plasma torch (1400) rated to 60.8 MPa (6,000 m depth) bridging internal arc-shroud recuperation against 2.0°C deep-ocean seawater to sustain a 6,800 K hydro-sheathed plasma jet (1402).
39. The torch (1400) of claim 38, generating +196.4 We continuous self-recharging power via a Ti-6Al-4V pressure-compensated thermoelectric hull (1404).
40. The torch (1400) of claim 38, utilizing a 0.75 T magnetic nozzle (1406) to cut polymetallic sulfide nodules and subsea steel structures without umbilical power.

41. A zero-recoil asteroid microgravity plasma rock-splitter (1500) projecting a 5,400 K magnetically focused plasma needle (1502) to induce internal phyllosilicate steam spallation with <0.15 N axial recoil.
42. The rock-splitter (1500) of claim 41, further comprising a vacuum aspiration hood (1504) capturing liberated H2O, CO2, and Ni(CO)4 carbonyl vapors for >100% closed-loop fluid self-sufficiency.
43. The rock-splitter (1500) of claim 41, rejecting waste enthalpy through a 120 K shaded radiator (1506) to export +184.0 We continuous power.

44. An autonomous atmospheric terraforming spire (1600) housing an array of cavitation-plasma reactors (100) converting planetary CO2, N2, and regolith perchlorates into breathable O2, fertilizer, and solid carbon.
45. The spire (1600) of claim 44, generating +348.5 kWe continuous microgrid power across 1,000 cores against a -60°C Martian thermal sink.
46. The spire (1600) of claim 44, operable in terrestrial climate-restoration mode to mineralize 6,450 kg/day of atmospheric CO2 into stable carbonates.

47. A sub-glacial cryo-volcanic melt and abyssal rover (1700) utilizing 33.6 kV acoustic-cavitation plasma fracturing (1702) to penetrate multi-kilometer cryogenic ice shells and harvest hydrothermal vent heat.
48. The rover (1700) of claim 47, hardened to 10^8 Gy with Sm2Co17 magnets, SOI electronics, and 4H-SiC betavoltaic liners (1704).
49. The rover (1700) of claim 47, generating +1,488 We during 95 K ice descent and +1,424 We during seafloor hydrothermal operation.

50. An evacuated maglev transit system (1800) wherein Cool Power Core reactors (1802) harvest vacuum roughing-pump compression heat and linear-stator losses against sub-surface earth or ocean cold sinks.
51. The transit system (1800) of claim 50, wherein 400 cores per kilometer offset >82% of steady-state tube vacuum maintenance power.
52. The transit system (1800) of claim 50, configured as a positively buoyant submerged transoceanic conduit (1900) tethered 150–300 m below sea level by tension-leg suction caissons (1902).
53. The submerged conduit (1900) of claim 52, maintaining abyssal thermal plume rise <= +0.08 K at 1.0 m and radiated acoustic noise below 92 dB re 1 uPa.
54. The submerged conduit (1900) of claim 52, incorporating 6-DOF seismic gimbals (1904) surviving Mw 9.2 fault displacement up to 6.5 m.
55. The transit system (1800) of claim 50, wherein passenger pods integrate zero-discharge onboard cabin life-support cores (1804) eliminating trackside sewage dump stations.

56. A floating ocean sanctuary and zero-brine desalination hub (2000) supported by pre-tensioned spar pontoons (2002) bridging process heat against 2–4°C abyssal water via Cool Power Core arrays (2004).
57. The hub (2000) of claim 56, eliminating hypersaline brine outfall by crystallizing solid NaCl, Mg(OH)2, battery-grade Li2CO3, and amidoxime-eluted U3O8 (2006).
58. The hub (2000) of claim 56, integrating a -200 m submerged transoceanic maglev terminal (2008) beneath a Category-5 rated 21.5°C ETFE geodesic canopy (2010).

59. An orbital artificial-gravity habitat (2100) comprising counter-rotating torus rings (2102) around a non-rotating cislunar mass-driver dock (2104) powered by Cool Power Core arrays (2106) rejecting heat to an 85 K shaded radiator (2108).
60. The habitat (2100) of claim 59, harvesting secondary cosmic-ray radiolytic flux (+21.5 We/core) within a 2.4 m water-wall radiation shield (2110).
61. The habitat (2100) of claim 59, achieving 99.85% closed-loop water recovery and 128.6% stoichiometric O2 regeneration for 5,000 residents.

62. A radiation-shielded linear ridge-and-valley subterranean megastructure (2200) having an aerodynamic 22°–26° outer hill profile covered by a 2.2–4.0 m living soil/forest mantle (2202), staggered sunlit canyon terraces (2204), and a multi-level subterranean commerce canyon (2206) powered by Cool Power Core arrays (2208).

64. The megastructure (2200) of claim 62, wherein the subterranean commerce canyon (2206) houses dual-bore evacuated maglev transit (2210) and automated pneumatic-shuttle pantry delivery.

65. A method of rehabilitating degraded strip-mines, alkali playas, or permafrost barrens by constructing the linear ridge-and-valley megastructure (2200) of claim 62 with zero virgin habitat displacement.
66. The method of claim 65, using nanosecond pulsed plasma reactors (2208) to mineralize acid mine drainage or thermokarst methane plumes while exporting net grid electricity and pure water.
67. The method of claim 65, utilizing sub-surface geothermal foundation piles (2212) to maintain year-round 21.5°C / 48% RH interior comfort without permafrost thaw or aquifer depletion.

68. A kinetic and directed-energy-harvesting exoskeleton armor assembly (2400) comprising an outer Bragg-mirror and B4C ceramic layer (2402), a 4H-SiC thermophotovoltaic and thermoelectric layer (2404), an open-cell viscoelastic zero-bounce foam layer with embedded piezoelectric PVDF-TrFE lattice (2406), and a 37°C micro-channel cooling liner (2408) coupled to a Cool Power Core (2410).

69. The armor assembly (2400) of claim 68, wherein the viscoelastic foam layer (2406) exhibits a coefficient of restitution e <= 0.035 and converts >96% of ballistic impact energy into electrical and thermal charge.

70. The armor assembly (2400) of claim 68, wherein the Bragg-mirror and 4H-SiC TPV layer (2402, 2404) reflect >92% of incident laser energy while converting absorbed thermal flux into +640 to +1,850 We return-fire supercapacitor power.

71. An atmospheric-condensing tri-mode return-fire weapon (2500) drawing harvested power and -78°C cryogenic cooling from the armor assembly (2400) of claim 68 to fire magnetically pinched plasma bolts, pulsed laser bursts, and cryo-sintered atmospheric particulate slugs.

72. The weapon (2500) of claim 71, comprising an 18,000 RPM cyclonic intake (2502), a -78°C cryogenic condensation mold (2504), a 33.6 kV plasma-sintering arc (2506), and a linear induction coilgun barrel (2508) accelerating 14.5 g slugs to 1,420 m/s.
73. The weapon (2500) of claim 71, operable in terrestrial N2/O2/dust and Martian CO2/regolith atmospheres without pre-manufactured solid ammunition magazines.

74. A quad-mode atmospheric-condensing weapon system (2600) combining the tri-mode atmospheric-slug, plasma-bolt, and pulsed-laser barrel (2500) of claim 71 with an under-barrel magnetically confined plasma bayonet emitter (2602) coupled to an onboard closed-loop Cool Power Core (2604).

75. The weapon system (2600) of claim 74, wherein the plasma bayonet emitter (2602) comprises a 0.38 T Sm2Co17 Halbach ring (2606) and a +0.24 T CuCrZr/CVD-diamond Bitter electromagnet coil (2608) projecting a 0.38 m, 4,450 K to 5,600 K chisel-point plasma blade.

76. The weapon system (2600) of claim 74, further comprising a closed-loop Bitter-coil cooling jacket (2610) routing +620 Wth of waste heat into the 90°C cavitation reservoir of the onboard Cool Power Core (2604) to pre-mold cryo-sintered slugs and export +318.4 to +348.0 We continuous power.

77. The weapon system (2600) of claim 74, incorporating a capacitive smart-grip deadman sensor (2612) executing solid-state GaN magnetic quench of the plasma bayonet in <0.9 milliseconds upon release.

abstract.p: A closed-loop thermodynamic cavitation and nanosecond pulsed plasma reactor (100) converts waste, metabolic, solar, geothermal, radiolytic, or directed-energy thermal differentials into continuous net electrical power (+286.0 to +368.5 We/core) and ultra-pure distilled condensate (12.96 L/day/core) while mineralizing 99.9999% of PFAS, pathogens, and hazardous gases. A 90°C fluid reservoir (102) feeds a CVD-graphene vortex cavitation chamber (104) and a 33.6 kV zero-voltage-switching nanosecond plasma discharge zone (106) coupled to a phase-change condenser (108). Modular architectures scale from wearable exoskeletons (500), tri-necked robotic mounts (800), kinetic/DEW-harvesting power armor (2400), and quad-mode atmospheric-condensing plasma-bayonet rifles (2600) to zero-septic homes (200), evacuated transoceanic maglev conduits (1900), radiation-shielded subterranean ridge cities (2200), floating zero-brine ocean hubs (2000), and orbital or planetary habitats (1600, 2100).
